title: Faithful LLM-Assisted Question Answering for Technical and Academic Search
authors: Juan Luis Filgueiras
source_name: International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR)
abstract: Technology scouting and competitive intelligence increasingly rely on rapid access to scientific and technical evidence. Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping question answering by enabling users to express exploratory and evolving information needs in natural language. However, their usefulness is limited by hallucinations, weak calibration, poor abstention when evidence is missing, and the cost of keeping knowledge up to date. In such settings, the key question is whether LLM-generated answers can be trusted for decision support, that is, whether they are faithful to available evidence, transparent about uncertainty, and easy to verify. Recent work shows that hallucinations remain pervasive, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has become the main strategy for grounding answers in external evidence. Yet even strong RAG systems often cite unsupported claims or generate plausible but fabricated references, especially under poor retrieval conditions. In response, prior work has examined citation faithfulness, decomposed generations into checkable units, and proposed factuality verification models and benchmarks. Still, the literature underexplores how to filter and validate evidence when sources are sparse, conflicting, or rapidly changing, as is common in technical and academic search. This thesis addresses that gap by studying faithful LLM-assisted question answering for technical and academic search as an end-to-end problem spanning collection construction, model adaptation, grounded generation, evidence verification, and user-centered evaluation. It is organized around five questions: how LLMs can support exploratory search beyond keywords; how retrieval and generation pipelines can produce trustworthy responses; how systems should behave when evidence is sparse or unreliable; how usefulness and trustworthiness should be evaluated; and which architectures and optimization strategies enable reliable real-world deployment. The thesis argues that truthful technical search requires explicit mechanisms for claim-level grounding, calibrated abstention, contradiction handling, and support-aware evidence presentation. Methodologically, the work follows a pipeline perspective in which datasets, models, and evaluation procedures co-evolve. The empirical setup combines public QA and RAG benchmarks with technical and scientific collections tailored to technology scouting scenarios. A central methodological contribution will be the design of scenario-based evaluation subsets targeting null-retrieval, conflicting evidence, noisy or weak-signal evidence, and exploratory information needs. On top of these resources, the thesis will compare single-pass RAG and more structured agentic pipelines while varying retrieval strategies, prompting policies, claim-evidence alignment procedures, quotation and citation behaviors, and model adaptation techniques such as instruction tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and reinforcement-based optimization. Evaluation will be multi-dimensional. In addition to answer utility and retrieval effectiveness, the thesis will measure citation faithfulness, support coverage, hallucination and false citation rates, abstention quality, uncertainty communication, and robustness under perturbed retrieval conditions. Whenever feasible, these automatic analyses will be complemented with analyst-oriented user studies that examine whether different evidence presentation formats help users reduce verification cost in realistic scouting workflows. Overall, the expected contribution is a principled and deployable framework for trustworthy natural-language access to scientific and technical information, combining faithful generation, verifiable evidence selection, and evaluation protocols tailored to real technical and academic search.

title: Inqeduagent: Adaptive AI Learning Partners with Gaussian Process Augmentation
authors: Wen-Xi Yang; Tian-Fang Zhao; Guan Liu
source_name: Asia Conference on Machine Learning and Computing (ACMLC)
abstract: Collaborative partnerships play a crucial role in inquiry-oriented education. However, most learning partners are currently assigned through experience-driven heuristics or rule-based machine assistants, which often result in limited knowledge expansion and low adaptability. To address these challenges, this study introduces InqEduAgent, an LLM-empowered generative agent framework designed to simulate and select adaptive learning partners for inquiry-based learning. InqEduAgent integrates a Gaussian process-augmented matching mechanism to model the cognitive and evaluative characteristics of learners, allowing adaptive partner selection based on prior knowledge patterns. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that InqEduAgent consistently achieves superior performance across diverse learning scenarios and large language model configurations. This study advances human-AI collaborative learning by enabling intelligent pairing between human- and AI-based learning partners, and contributes to adaptive user modeling and personalized recommendation within Web-based educational environments.

title: Knowledge-Informed Primary School Layout Planning via RAG-Based Multimodal LLMs
authors: Weishi Zhou; Lu Gao; Minglai Chen; Xin Song Li; Pengpeng Liang; Gen Yang; Jiang Wen; Zhenshan Jin
source_name: International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning (PRML)
abstract: Automated architectural layout planning for primary school campuses presents a highly constrained optimization challenge, requiring simultaneous adherence to functional zoning principles and national regulatory standards. Existing GAN-based approaches operate at the pixel level and frequently produce layouts that are visually coherent yet functionally deficient-a limitation we term semantic blindness. To address this gap, we propose a Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhanced Multimodal Large Language Model (RAG-MLLM) framework that grounds generation in structured domain knowledge. The framework encodes the Code for Design of Schools (GB 50099-2011) into a FAISS-indexed vector store of 87 regulatory clauses, dynamically retrieved at inference time and injected into a threelayer prompt—comprising Role, Task, and Constraint components—submitted to Gemini 3.1 Flash Image for cross-modal spatial reasoning. Experiments on the Open SCUT-AutoALP dataset show that a double-blind expert evaluation confirms a 33.4% improvement in Functional Completeness and a 7.7% gain in Spatial Rationality over the Pix2PixHD baseline, with distributional analysis further corroborating closer alignment to professional design norms. These results demonstrate the potential of knowledge-driven generation for regulation-critical architectural typologies.

title: Skill-Grounded LLM Agents for Dynamic Dashboard Generation in Water Conservancy Consultation
authors: Miao Yu; Hao Liu; Min Chen; Huining Jiang; Jun Hou
abstract: Water conservancy consultation requires rapid integration and analysis of multi-source heterogeneous data, which places high demands on the flexibility, responsiveness, and intelligence of visual dashboard systems. However, traditional large-screen dashboards are typically built with fixed layouts and manually configured data bindings, making them difficult to adapt to temporary consultation needs and ad hoc data queries. To address this issue, this paper proposes an LLM-driven method for intelligent orchestration and dynamic generation of visual dashboards for water conservancy consultation. The proposed method formalizes visualization components as structured Skills and organizes them in a Skill registry, enabling a large language model agent to understand component semantics, applicable scenarios, data requirements, and layout constraints. Given a natural language consultation request, the agent automatically performs requirement analysis, component selection, layout planning, and Text-to-SQL generation, producing a complete dashboard configuration without manual drag-and-drop operations. Experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly reduce dashboard generation time and support ad hoc expert queries with second-level response. The approach provides an effective solution for intelligent and adaptive decision-support dashboards in water conservancy management.

title: Diagnostic Reasoning with Large Language Models for a Rare Disease: Case Study of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia
authors: Swati Rajwal; Mary Ellen Fain; Lokesh Guglani; Abeed Sarker
source_name: Language Resources and Evaluation Conference (LREC)
abstract: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare pediatric lung disease that is frequently underdiagnosed due to nonspecific early symptoms and limited clinical exposure.We investigate whether large language models (LLMs) can support early diagnostic reasoning using real-world pediatric pulmonology notes written before the final diagnosis.We curated 58 de-identified first-visit notes (28 confirmed PCD, 30 controls) and evaluated five open-source LLMs using a standardized zero-shot prompt to produce structured outputs, including PCD evaluation recommendations, justifications, and suggested tests.Quantitative performance was assessed against expert-validated labels using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, and a clinician qualitatively reviewed all explanations and testing recommendations for clinical soundness.Sensitivity ranged from 0.48 to 1.00 and specificity from 0.10 to 0.48 (excluding uncertain outputs), with a best accuracy of 0.75.A majority-vote ensemble of five open-source LLMs achieved perfect sensitivity (1.00) with accuracy of 0.73.While models often identified clinically relevant signals in unstructured notes, explanations and testing recommendations were frequently only partially sound.These findings suggest LLMs may serve as cautious early screening aids for rare disease suspicion, but not as standalone diagnostic tools.This work further highlights the need for larger, multi-site evaluation on longitudinal clinical text.

title: Artificial Intelligence in French Healthcare and Emergency Response: A Multi-Site Case Study from Predictive Modeling to Generative AI
authors: Roxane Elias Mallouhy; Christophe Guyeux
source_name: International Conference on Machine Learning Technologies (ICMLT)
abstract: This paper presents two operational case studies of Artificial Intelligence (AI) deployment in French healthcare and emergency response systems: the ARS BourgogneFranche-Comté (BFC) predictive analytics platform and the Marcus/IAppel emergency call management project. The ARS BFC initiative, operational since 2018 across approximately fifty healthcare facilities, employs XGBoost-based forecasting models achieving Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 5-6 admissions/day for hospitalizations and 12-13 admissions/day for overall ED visits across 1 to 14-day horizons. The platform integrates digital twin technology for simulation-based strategic planning. The Marcus project, piloted in the Ain department with 40 real emergency calls analyzed, implements a multi-stage AI pipeline combining automatic speech recognition (Whisper), named entity recognition, and large language model classification, achieving F1-scores exceeding 93% for urgency detection. Both initiatives demonstrate a human-augmentation paradigm where AI assists rather than replaces operators. We document the technical architectures, quantitative performance metrics, user feedback, and lessons learned from multi-year deployments, addressing practical challenges including data governance, algorithmic limitations for rare events, and regulatory alignment with the EU AI Act.

title: KARM: Knowledge-Augmented Reagent Management for Digitalized Biological Supply Chains with an Evolvable Graph
authors: Zhihua He; Arlo Octavia
source_name: International Conference on Digital Society and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI)
abstract: Effective management of biological reagent supply chains is challenged by product selection complexity, fragmented supplier information, and the demand for cost-effective domestic alternatives. We introduce KARM, a framework centered on a continuously evolving Reagent Knowledge Graph (RKG) that acquires multimodal knowledge from product catalogs, scientific literature, and supplier images via a confidence-weighted pipeline with explicit error-propagation control, parses procurement queries into structured constraint tuples for subgraph retrieval, and employs a Graph Neural Network combining multi-objective cost-of-ownership scoring with graph-derived substitution signals. The RKG evolves through bias-aware procurement feedback, enabling community-validated product equivalence learning. A cold-start module handles newly launched reagents lacking procurement history. On a 500-query biological reagent benchmark, KARM achieves 91.2% constraint match—outperforming monolithic LLM baselines by 22.9% and clarification-enhanced baselines by 15.8%—with cold-start recovery reaching 84.3%. Ablations confirm the necessity of every component for supply chain optimization.

title: Generative AI for Demand Forecasting and Strategic Supply Chain Planning in Automotive/FMCG Industries: An Interactive Hybrid Framework to Time Series Analysis and Large Language Models
authors: Asif Ahmed J; Ranjith Kumar R; Sandhya Sasidharan; J. Priya; S. Subbalakshmi
source_name: International Conference on Trends in Quantum Computing and Emerging Business Technologies (TQCEBT)
abstract: Proper forecasting of the demand and supply chain planning are irreplaceable in the automotive and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sectors in terms of operational efficiency. Traditional forecasting models have many limitations on their flexibility to disruptions in real time and capabilities to provide decision support in an interpretable form as they are largely dependent upon historical numeric information and statistical models. The paper is a proposal of a hybridization of the artificial intelligence systems that combines time-series prediction with domain-specific generative reasoning to support disruption-aware demand forecasting and strategic supply chain planning. Facebook Prophet can be used to model trend, seasonality, and holiday trends in past sales data and real-time disruption indicators (logistics delays, weather anomalies, and supplier constraints) are added through external application programming interfaces. The refined numerical predictions are converted into comprehensive advice that is readable by people using a domain adapted large language model (LLM), which has undergone training with supply chain specific prompts and contextual knowledge. The framework is assessed on automotive and FMCG data in the real world. Empirical outcomes show that using experiments result into substantial improvements on forecast accuracy, stockout reduction and a higher level of interpretability when compared to the traditional statistical and deep-learning methodologies. The results highlight the usefulness of using predictive analytics with domain-specific generative artificial intelligence to produce explainable and data-driven supply chain optimization.

title: A Dual-Roofline Runtime Model for Capacity Planning in Shared-Backend LLM Multi-Agent Social Simulation: A Case Study of AgentSociety
authors: Xiaoyang Chang; Sichen Tao; Masatoshi Kawai; Hiroyuki Takizawa
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent social simulations are jointly shaped by message frequency, cognitive inference, and shared-backend queueing, yet still lack interpretable runtime models. Using AgentSociety’s fixed-step social simulation as a case study, we model the average step time of a complete run with a dual-Roofline formulation: the cognitive phase and the message phase are treated as two resource-bounded regions sharing one vLLM backend, and the saturation point of each phase is determined by the per-GPU token budget divided by the measured average prompt length. Call-level traces and source-code inspection show that the message-dispatch stage is not pure routing but includes message-triggered LLM decisions. Ray scheduling remains at only 1.8–2.4ms, whereas mean vLLM service time rises from 0.30s to 1.63s as the agent count grows from 5 to 500, confirming that shared inference throughput and cross-phase queueing are the dominant bottlenecks. We therefore decompose total step time into environment overhead, a cognitive Roofline, a message Roofline, and a cross-phase queueing term. Compared with a linear model, a single Roofline, and a dual Roofline without queueing, the full model reduces mean absolute error from 8.6%, 2.4%, and 1.2% to 0.7%. Across eight scale points spanning 4 to 500 agents, the model achieves R2=0.9999 and reveals three regimes: compute-bound, message-saturated, and fully saturated with cross-phase queueing. It further yields two practical capacity-planning rules: at large scale, message frequency should be the first control lever; for the 500-agent setting, about 10 replicas remove superlinear growth and about 27 replicas recover an almost constant-step regime. These results show that analytic performance modeling can bridge the gap between large-scale LLM multi-agent simulation and practical infrastructure capacity planning, contributing to the systems foundation of intelligent social computing.

title: Zero-Shot Multi-Reference Personalization via MLLMs-Guided Layout Planning
authors: Junhao Feng
abstract: Though zero-shot adapters excel in image personalization, they often encounter significant challenges in multi-reference personalized generation, specifically failing to precisely adhere to the spatial layouts described in text prompts and suffering from feature leakage between reference images. To address these two challenges, we propose RIG (Regional Image-prompt Generation), a novel training-free framework. For the first challenge, leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), we introduce a layout planning binder. Leveraging Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, this module infers and generates precise global layouts from text prompts, while simultaneously binding reference images to their corresponding regions. For the second, we introduce a satially decoupled diffusion mechanism that isolates feature streams during attention computation. By injecting reference features exclusively into designated regions, this mechanism effectively prevents feature interference between reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RIG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art adapter methods in terms of both personalization fidelity and text-layout alignment.

title: Redefining Middle Management: How Generative AI Reshapes Roles and Competencies
authors: Philippe Jean-Baptiste
source_name: Lecture notes in networks and systems
abstract: This ongoing research investigates how Generative AI (GAI) reshapes the roles and competencies of middle managers. While most work targets macro-level impacts, we focus on micro-level changes in adaptation, decision-making, and skill reconfiguration. Using activity theory and an inductive qualitative design, we analyze 60 semi-structured interviews with middle managers from three contrasting contexts: a large energy enterprise, a medium-sized digital services firm, and a small telecommunications company. The multi-site setup enables comparison across governance models and cultures. Preliminary results show middle managers often lead GAI experimentation, initiating bottom-up innovations outside official IT channels. These shadow practices accelerate problem-solving yet create risks around data protection, compliance, and strategic drift. Beyond automating routine work, GAI supports cognitive structuring, altering how managers plan, communicate, and lead. The findings point to hybrid competencies that extend beyond technical literacy: conceptual skills (sense-making, systems thinking), human skills (empathy, leadership, conflict mediation), and ethical awareness. Middle managers emerge as pivotal translators between frontline innovation and top-down strategy. The paper contributes a multi-dimensional account of managerial transformation through the lens of activity theory and offers actionable guidance for responsible GAI integration: adaptive governance, targeted upskilling, and protected “safe-to-experiment” spaces. Future work will expand the dataset and trace longitudinal trajectories of adoption and governance.

title: Finding the Perfect Research Collaborator: Partner Selection Based on Technological Fit
authors: Benjamin Vehmeyer; Michaela Geierhos
source_name: Lecture notes in networks and systems
abstract: Although collaborative research is vital to innovation, identifying suitable partners is challenging due to fragmented data and limited matching methods. Traditional approaches often focus narrowly on patent-based similarity, which excludes non-patenting institutions and fails to consider the specific intent of research projects. We present a novel hybrid system for matching research partners that combines semantic retrieval with structured technology classification. Our approach integrates three main components: (1) a semantic search framework that matches project descriptions to heterogeneous institutional data sources; (2) a two-step IPC-based profiling system that uses semantic retrieval and LLM refinement; and (3) a scoring mechanism that balances similarity, complementarity, and semantic proximity. This strategy enables context-aware, cross-sector partner recommendations tailored to the specific intent of research initiatives. A software prototype serves as an evaluation framework reviewed by experts. Preliminary evaluation shows a success rate of 69.2% at 10, indicating the practical utility of our hybrid approach.

title: Leveraging Generative AI and Digital Transformation for Achieving Business Sustainability in the Era of Net-Zero Goals
authors: Mayank Chhatwal; Shikha Kapoor; Namita Rajput; Vikas Garg
abstract: The global drive towards sustainability and net-zero emissions has reshaped the priorities of businesses worldwide, compelling them to integrate innovative technologies into their operations. This paper examines how generative artificial intelligence (AI), when combined with digital transformation, can act as a catalyst for achieving business sustainability in the era of net-zero goals. Generative AI technologies, such as advanced natural language processing models and image synthesis tools, are explored for their ability to foster eco-friendly innovation, enhance resource optimization, and provide predictive analytics for sustainability-oriented decision-making[1]. These technologies, integrated within broader digital transformation initiatives, enable organizations to redesign processes, reduce waste, and implement circular economy practices[2].Through case studies and emerging trends, the paper identifies practical applications where generative AI has successfully driven sustainability outcomes, such as energy management, supply chain optimization, and emissions tracking[3]. It also evaluates the critical challenges associated with adopting AI-driven solutions, including ethical considerations, data security concerns, and workforce adaptation to new technologies[4]. The research emphasizes the alignment of AI capabilities with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) goals, showcasing how businesses can achieve operational efficiency while addressing global sustainability challenges[5].

title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Risk Assessment in Hyperconnected Logistic Hub Network Deployment
authors: Yinzhu Quan; Yujia Xu; Guanlin Chen; Benoît Montreuil; IMT Mines Albi; Frédérick Bénaben
source_name: IISE Annual Conference & Expo
abstract: The growing emphasis on energy efficiency and environmental sustainability in global supply chains introduces new challenges in the deployment of hyperconnected logistics hubs. In such volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous (VUCA) logistics networks, risk assessment becomes essential to ensure successful hub deployment. However, traditional methods often struggle to effectively capture and analyze unstructured textual information. In this paper, we leverage large language models (LLMs) with tools to conduct risk assessment for logistics hub deployment. We use LLMs to identify potential risks by analyzing unstructured data, such as geopolitical factors, regulatory changes, and environmental risks. These data are integrated into tools, which can be automatically called by the LLMs to support our decision-making process. In addition, we design prompts to instruct LLMs to assess the feasibility of hub selection by analyzing risk types and levels, and then providing insights for hub location recommendations. Finally, we conduct a comparative analysis of new and existing hub locations to evaluate improvements in risk mitigation and overall network resilience.

title: LLM-empowered multi-agent intelligent planning for PV-EV penetrated distribution networks
authors: Shao, Kaiwen;Xiang, Yue;Li, Lingtao;Liu, Junyong
source_name: Applied Energy
abstract: The large-scale integration of distributed photovoltaics (PV) and electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) introduces severe congestion and voltage violations in urban distribution networks. Traditional planning methods heavily rely on physical grid expansion and centralized mathematical optimization, which fail to reconcile the inherent “zero-sum” economic conflicts among the Distribution System Operator (DSO), PV developers, and EVCS operators. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel cognitive-physical multi-agent collaborative planning framework empowered by Large Language Model (LLM). First, a generative multi-agent system is constructed to represent the diverse stakeholders. By leveraging the semantic understanding and logical reasoning of LLMs, the agents can dynamically perceive planning scenarios and user intents, auto-generating game-theoretic weights. Second, in the physical layer, an improved genetic algorithm with minimum spanning tree constraints (MST-IGA) is proposed, integrating real-world road-right-of-way data and time-series power flow simulations to ensure engineering feasibility. Furthermore, a “Cognitive Awakening” mechanism based on Non-Wires Alternatives (NWA) is introduced. Under extreme constraints, the LLM agents autonomously negotiate to deploy Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) rather than curtailing capacity, effectively transforming the investment deadlock into a positive-sum game. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed framework dynamically adapts to various scenarios. Compared to conventional heuristic methods, the LLM-driven multi-agent gaming strategy significantly reduces the DSO's physical capacity expansion costs, maximizes the PV hosting capacity, and provides highly explainable consensus blueprints for modern power system planning.

title: LLM-Stochastic Optimization Framework: Intelligent Supply Chain Planning with Uncertainty-Aware Inventory Control
authors: Zhou, Sihua;Zhou, Xing
source_name: Proceedings of 2026 7th International Conference on Computer Information and Big Data Applications Cibda 2026
abstract: Effective supply chain management under demand and lead-time uncertainties remains a critical challenge for modern enterprises seeking to balance customer service levels with operational costs. Existing approaches suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) inability to interpret complex natural language planning objectives and orchestrate multi-modal analytical workflows, (2) reliance on deterministic inventory models that inadequately capture stochastic supply-demand dynamics, and (3) lack of integrated frameworks bridging strategic decision-making with operational execution. To address these challenges, we propose LLM-SIO (LLM-Stochastic Inventory Optimization), a comprehensive AI-driven framework that synergistically combines large language model-based intelligent agents with simulation-based stochastic optimization. Our key innovations include: (1) a memory-augmented LLM agent architecture with retrieval-augmented generation for intent-driven task orchestration, (2) a two-stage stochastic programming formulation with Monte Carlo simulation for robust safety stock optimization under dual uncertainties, and (3) a closed-loop validation mechanism integrating offline policy search with online MRP execution. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset of 127 SKUs demonstrate that LLM-SIO achieves 94.2% service level with 18% cost reduction compared to baseline methods, validating its effectiveness for intelligent supply chain planning.

title: Routine physics work efficacy and efficiency improvement through a shared-duty physicist-of-the-day model in a multi-hospital radiation oncology network
authors: Chen, Guang Pei;Prah, Douglas E.;Paulson, Eric S.
source_name: Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics
abstract: Background: Large multi-hospital radiation oncology networks often rely on site-exclusive physicist coverage models that can lead to imbalanced workload distribution, inconsistent task execution, communication fragmentation, and vulnerability to delayed or missed quality checks. Increasing clinical complexity and distributed staffing models necessitate operational strategies that improve efficiency, standardization, and safety across geographically separated sites. Purpose: To describe the implementation of a shared-duty physicist-of-the-day (POD) model supported by a real-time operational dashboard and to evaluate its impact on workload distribution, task efficiency, and safety metrics across a multi-hospital radiation oncology network. Methods: A structural transition from a site-exclusive to a shared-duty POD model was implemented in our institution—a four-site academic radiation oncology system. A custom application, RadOncStatusBoard, was developed using structured query language (SQL)-based integration with the Mosaiq Record & Verify system to aggregate real-time patient appointments, treatment progress, quality checklist (QCL) items, and weekly chart check (WCC) eligibility. Microsoft Teams channels were used for daily communication and task coordination. Operational data from two matched 21-month intervals—before and after POD restructuring—were extracted using SQL. Evaluated metrics included task volumes, claim times, completion times, WCC performance, billing accuracy, and dosimetry-related Radiation Oncology Incident Learning System (RO-ILS) event reporting. Right-skewed distributions were summarized using medians and interquartile ranges (IQR). Surveys of physicists and dosimetrists were performed to assess end-user perceptions of workflow and safety. Results: Workload balance improved across all task categories, with substantial decreases in main-to-satellite task ratios (e.g., the ratio for chart close decreased from 1.91 to 1.27). Task claim and completion times decreased markedly at both main and satellite locations (e.g., chart-close claim time decreased from 36.8 to 6.2 min at the main campus). WCC completion improved from 97.7% to 99.9%, and WCC charge capture increased from 96.1% to 99.4%. The proportion of dosimetry-related RO-ILS events decreased numerically from 31.0% to 26.7% (p = 0.339). Survey responses from physicists and dosimetrists indicated improved workflow clarity, communication, workload balance, and perceived patient safety. Conclusions: Implementation of a shared-duty POD model improved workload balance, enhanced operational efficiency, and strengthened routine safety processes across a multi-site radiation oncology program. Integration of a real-time operational dashboard, standardized communication pathways, and structured task-claiming workflows enabled measurable gains in responsiveness, compliance, and perceived safety culture.

title: Advancing the calibration of macroscale hydrological models by integrating sensitivity analysis, adaptive pseudo-modeling optimization and multi-site calibration
authors: Thakur, Chandni;Budamala, Venkatesh;Kasiviswanathan, K. S.;Teutschbein, Claudia;Soundharajan, Bankaru Swamy
source_name: Journal of Hydrology
abstract: Accurate estimation of parameters in macroscale, complex hydrological models (HMs) using effective calibration procedures can improve the characterization of real-world phenomena of hydrological fluxes. This study presents a novel, model-agnostic calibration framework that integrates global sensitivity analysis (SA) with an adaptive pseudo-modelling optimization strategy. The framework is designed to overcome key limitations of conventional calibration methods, such as reliance on exhaustive one-shot sampling, absence of formal parameter screening, and restriction to single site calibration. To demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework, catchment-specific sensitive parameters of the variable infiltration capacity model (VIC) with a 0.15° spatial resolution were calibrated for streamflow simulations over the Godavari River basin in India using both single- and multi-site calibration. An ensemble of pseudo models, including Gaussian process regression, kriging, and artificial neural networks, was employed to enhance robustness and generalization. Although the performance indicators (NSE, KGE ≥ 0.8 and PBIAS ≤ 15) in both scenarios demonstrated similar model performance at the catchment outlet, scenario 2 outperformed single-site calibration in terms of equifinality reduction, less parameter uncertainty and improved computational efficiency. By combining Sobol SA, ensemble pseudo modelling, and multi-site calibration, the framework efficiently explored hydrologically relevant regions of the parameter space, reduced dimensionality by excluding non-influential parameters, and lowered overall computational burden. The proposed framework is a robust method for improving the simulation capability of macroscale HMs under diverse hydroclimatic conditions. Plain language summary: Hydrological models, such as the VIC model, are powerful computer-based tools used to study and understand water movement on a local to large scale, particularly at the river basin scale. The calibration process involves adjusting the model’s parameters to ensure that the model outputs align with real-world observations. Improving the calibration of hydrological models, like VIC, enhances their ability to make reliable predictions, which is vital for effective water resource management and decision-making. This paper presents a novel hybrid modelling framework combining sensitivity analysis and an adaptive optimization algorithm to calibrate complex hydrological models automatically. The proposed approach can be a robust and time-efficient method for improving large-scale hydrological models, enabling decision-makers to make informed choices and develop effective strategies for addressing water-related challenges.

title: Developing creative reading skills through graphic organizers among Saudi EFL learners
authors: Barashid, Majed
source_name: Frontiers in Education
abstract: Although creative reading is a core higher-order literacy skill, it remains one of the most neglected dimensions of reading pedagogy in English as a foreign language (EFL), and no previous experimental study has examined the effect of systematic graphic organizer instruction on creative reading skills in Saudi higher education. This study addressed that gap by investigating the effect of a graphic organizers-based instructional program on Saudi EFL students' creative reading skills. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 43 male freshmen EFL students at Al-Jouf College of Technology in Saudi Arabia, randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 22) taught through five types of graphic organizers (Venn diagram, Know–Want to Know–Learned [KWL] chart, concept mapping, fishbone diagram, and circle map) over eight weeks, and a control group (n = 21) that received conventional instruction. A validated creative reading skills test measured four sub-skills: originality, flexibility, fluency, and elaboration. title: A scalable AI-Based system for evaluating and enhancing responsible media coverage of suicide: A multi-site, multi-language implementation study
authors: Levi-Belz, Y.;Nobile, B.;Levkovich, I.;Courtet, P.;Elyoseph, Z.
source_name: Computers in Human Behavior Reports
abstract: Background Irresponsible media coverage of suicide can increase suicide rates through the “Werther effect,” while responsible reporting can reduce risk and stigma. Although the WHO has issued clear guidelines for responsible reporting, adherence remains inconsistent worldwide due to structural barriers and the lack of real-time tools for journalists. This study aimed to develop and rigorously evaluate a multilingual GenAI-based system that can automatically assess and enhance suicide-related news articles to align with WHO guidelines, offering a scalable pathway for more responsible coverage. Methods A total of 120 suicide-related articles (English, Hebrew, and French) were systematically selected and independently evaluated for guideline adherence by both expert human raters and the AI system. The articles were automatically revised using the AI correction module. Post-enhancement, all articles were re-evaluated by the system and by a new set of human raters to compare changes in adherence levels. Results The AI system demonstrated high agreement with human raters at baseline (ICC = .77), with slight conservative bias in some languages. Following the AI-based enhancement bot, both AI and human evaluations confirmed significant improvements in guideline adherence (mean scores increased from ∼45% to ∼85%), with no significant post-enhancement differences between human and AI ratings. Conclusions This study provides initial empirical support for using GenAI to automatically evaluate and enhance suicide-related media coverage across languages and contexts. By offering journalists a practical, real-time tool for producing accurate, ethically sound content, this approach can help mitigate suicide contagion, increase public awareness, and foster a global metric for responsible reporting.

title: Large-scale tethered screen of RNA-binding proteins reveals novel regulators of poly(A) site selection
authors: Jagannatha, Pratibha;Yoon, Yoseop;Landry, Samuel B.;Naritomi, Jack T.;Zhan, Lijun;Olson, Sara;Wei, Xintao;Street, Lena A.;Liu, Liang;Jeong, Joshua;Quan, Cailyx;Reid, Jack;Soles, Lindsey V.;Segeberg, Max;Schmok, Jonathan C.;Jain, Manya;Rosales, Elijah K.F.;Chen, Vicky W.;Gosztyla, Maya L.;Xu, Shuhao;Pong, Avery;Jovanovic, Marko;Graveley, Brenton R.;Shi, Yongsheng;Yeo, Gene W.
source_name: Molecular Cell
abstract: Alternative polyadenylation (APA) generates transcript isoforms with distinct 3′ ends, yet the repertoire of its protein regulators remains poorly defined. Using a large-scale tethered function screen, we profiled 879 human RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) and identified 63 high-confidence activators of poly(A) site (PAS) selection, most of which were not previously linked to APA. We validated these factors by knockdown PAS-seq, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and enhanced cross-linking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) analyses and developed a fine-tuned protein language model that predicts PAS selection activators and their key functional domains. We then mechanistically dissected two unexpected hits: GRB2, a signaling adaptor protein, and RNPS1, a peripheral component of the exon junction complex (EJC). Both regulate APA, at least in part, through direct interactions with distinct subunits of the cleavage and polyadenylation (CPA) machinery. Together, our study provides a comprehensive resource of APA-regulating RBPs and uncovers unexpected roles of signaling and EJC factors in APA regulation.

title: Generating Databases from Natural Language Specification
authors: Mitra, Aviroop;Sanghi, Anupam
source_name: Proceedings of the Workshop on Synthetic Data Generation and Management for Building AI Systems Synthai 2026 Co Located with SIGMOD Companion 2026
abstract: Synthetic databases are critical for application development, testing, benchmarking, and data engineering workflows. Existing database generators typically require formal specifications, significant technical expertise, or access to production datasets and workloads, making them unsuitable for rapid bootstrapping in greenfield settings. This makes them unsuitable for domain experts seeking rapid bootstrapping in greenfield design settings. To address this, we present ScribbleDB, an end-to-end agentic pipeline that converts natural language descriptions into database schemas and instantiated tables. The pipeline decomposes the task into four stages: fact extraction, schema generation, constraint modeling and code generation. The pipeline consists of four stages: fact extraction, schema generation, constraint modeling, and code generation. By combining LLM-based reasoning with deterministic validation and large-scale materialization, ScribbleDB avoids scalability bottlenecks in schema complexity and data size. Experiments show that ScribbleDB achieves nearly six-fold higher table accuracy and fourfold lower latency than prior work across multiple datasets, while preserving statistical realism and logical fidelity.

title: Enabling Non-Simulation Experts to Adapt Digital Twins during Production System Redesign using Agentic AI
authors: Schwede, Christian;Schipper, Lennart;Cirullies, Jan
source_name: Iccmb 2026 Proceedings of 2026 the 9th International Conference on Computers in Management and Business
abstract: Simulation-based digital twins are a core foundation for the efficient and holistic optimization of material-flow systems across the lifecycle - from design and planning to control. However, constructing digital representations of supply chains and production/logistics systems is labor-intensive and largely manual. Current research seeks to shift from manual expert modeling to auto-generated digital twins derived from event-log data using process mining and machine learning. Yet, structural adaptation of these models during (re)design typically still requires intervention by simulation experts. This paper presents an approach that enables structural adaptation of digital-twin models during redesign via an LLM-based design assistant, which performs modeling through natural-language interaction with non-expert users. The assistant employs an agentic, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflow and relies exclusively on publicly available information from the open-source digital-twin platform OpenFactoryTwin (OFacT) to execute adaptations. The proposed framework is evaluated in an empirical study based on data from an IoT-Factory - a laboratory assembly environment.

This platform is based on natural language processing and machine learning technologies, supporting automated lesson preparation, recommendation of lesson preparation materials and design of classroom teaching activities. title: An AI-based chatbot to support health-related social needs among pediatric primary care population: Protocol for a pilot randomized controlled trial
authors: Sezgin, Emre;Clarkson, Elizabeth;Logan, Faith;Jackson, Daniel I.;Hussain, Syed Amad;Stokes, Joshua;Bunger, Alicia;Brock, Guy;Fosler-Lussier, Eric;Kemper, Alex R.;Pai, Ahna L.
source_name: Plos One
abstract: Unmet health-related social needs (HRSNs) are major drivers of poor health outcomes in early childhood. Children with unmet HRSNs are at greater risk for developmental delays, caregiver stress, and increased healthcare utilization, yet current screening approaches in pediatric primary care are resource-intensive and inconsistently implemented. AI-powered chatbots (conversational agents or virtual assistants) may offer a private, secure, scalable, and cost-effective alternative for identifying unmet needs and connecting families to services. This protocol describes a pilot randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and usability of DAPHNE, an AI-driven chatbot developed to facilitate the identification of unmet HRSNs and provide personalized community resource referrals. One hundred caregivers of children under two years of age will be recruited from Nationwide Children’s Hospital pediatric primary care clinics and randomized to either the standard care (control) group or DAPHNE+ Standard care (intervention) group (n = 50 each arm). Caregivers will complete surveys at baseline, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention (depending on the measure). For the intervention group, participants will receive weekly chatbot prompts and on-demand access throughout the 6-month study period. Primary outcomes include study feasibility (recruitment, retention, and survey completion across both arms), acceptability (caregiver-reported ratings in both arms and intervention-specific ratings), and usability of the DAPHNE chatbot (System Usability Scale among intervention participants). Secondary outcomes includes caregiver-reported outcome measures (caregiver stress, self-efficacy, satisfaction with resource access, quality of life), and electronic health record-derived measures (including documentation of HRSN screening and referrals, adherence to well-child visits, missed appointments, emergency department utilization, and estimated healthcare costs). In addition, ten primary care providers will also participate to assess workflow integration and report on current HRSN practices. Mixed-methods analyses will integrate survey data, chatbot engagement metrics, and qualitative interviews to refine both the intervention and the study protocol. The results of this study will inform the design of a future multi-site trial to evaluate the efficacy and implementation of DAPHNE for addressing HRSNs in pediatric primary care. Trial registration: NCT07168382.

title: Intelligent supply chain control towers
authors: Vlachos, Ilias
source_name: Encyclopedia in Operations Management
abstract: This chapter presents the development of an intelligent supply chain control tower (iSCCT). Despite the developments in artificial intelligence (AI), including generalized AI, like Large Language Models (LLMs), few companies know how to use them to transform their traditional supply chains (SCs).This chapter presents key capabilities of iSCCT, i.e., Intelligent Visibility, Supply Chain Automation and Process Optimization, SC risk management, SC Planning and Execution. It demonstrates how a company (Zeta) transformed its supply chain into a 3-stage evolution: (1) Learning, where Zeta acquired knowledge from outsourcing the SCTT to its logistics partner. (2) Execution, where Zeta faced significant challenges, including software misalignments, poor internal integration, lack of top management support, and budget constraints. These challenges delayed the iSCCT implementation. Eventually, Zeta integrated Human, Operational, and Technological Intelligence into its iSCCT. (3) Growth phase, with increased automation and human-technology integration.The study shows how companies can internally develop an intelligent supply chain control tower. It discusses key takeaways for operations managers and researchers.

title: Energy-Aware Distributed Data-Center GPU Scheduling via Constrained Hybrid SAC with Adaptive Frequency
authors: Duc, Ma Viet;Duong, Nguyen Dang;Huy, Nguyen Duc;Tuyen, Nguyen Duc;Hung, Nguyen Tai;Thanh, Nguyen Huu
source_name: International Conference on Information Networking
abstract: AI training jobs increasingly arrive from multiple ingress points and must be placed across heterogeneous, geodistributed GPU data centers. In this scenario, energy use increases rapidly if schedulers overlook where to route, how many GPUs to allocate, and which frequency to use. We present CHSAC-AF (Constrained Hybrid Soft Actor-Critic with Adaptive Frequency), a learning-based scheduler that factorizes the discrete action into data-center choice and GPU-count selection with feasibility masks, and delegates per-site DVFS to a model-based oracle that picks the energy-optimal clock on the local discrete frequency set. Constraints on queue/latency are handled via a CMDP with dual updates, and distributional critics stabilize learning under heavy-tailed service times. In a WAN-connected simulation with heterogeneous GPU clusters, CHSAC-AF simultaneously improves capacity and efficiency, completing jobs up to 1.6 times faster than a default policy while reducing the average energy per unit of work by about 17% compared to the default baseline. The learned policy keeps queues stable by steering arrivals away from bottleneck sites and selecting just-enough GPUs with energy-appropriate frequencies, demonstrating that energy-aware scheduling need not sacrifice throughput or service quality in distributed GPU data centers.

title: Reliable LLM-Powered Decision Engines for Large-Scale Supply Chain Operations: Architecture, Safety, and Performance Guarantees
authors: Jingar, Nirmal Kumar
source_name: Proceedings International Conference on Advanced Systems and Emergent Technologies IC Aset 2026
abstract: Current large-scale supply chains are highly uncertain, dynamic, and disruption prone that are challenging to serve up timely and resilient decisions through traditional rulebased and optimization-only systems. The increasing supply of heterogeneous data sources, such as transactional demand signals and unstructured disruption report, presents a chance of intelligent systems, which could reason, adapt and optimize at the same time. A hybrid architecture that combines large language models (LLMs) with mathematical optimization, probabilistic forecasting, and safety-constrained decision filtering is proposed in this paper as a performance of a Decision Engine, which is called LLM-Powered Decision Engine (LLM-DE). In comparison to purely data-driven or heuristic solutions, LLM-DE integrates semantic reasoning with LLM with a set of performance and safety guarantees that allow safe decision-making in large-scale supply chain processes. The suggested framework enables the end-To-end decision making such as demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and transportation routing and disruption mitigation. The findings affirm that language-based reasoning combined with optimization and formal constraints can be used to come up with not only smarter but also safer and more scalable supply chain decisions. This research provides a new architecture, a complete pipeline of algorithm, and a formulation based on mathematical constructs of the operational decision systems incorporating LLM. The proposed model offers a pragmatic and theoretical basis of the next-generation intelligent supply chain infrastructures that can be implemented to work dependably in the face of uncertainty and massive complexity.

title: A Systematic Approach to Reducing Human Errors in Maintenance Processes Using Multi-Agents
authors: Qura, Ahmed;Ibrahim, Ahmed;Zalzala, Ali
source_name: 2026 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence Cai 2026
abstract: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly advanced artificial intelligence capabilities; nevertheless, a significant challenge persists in ensuring that LLMs can function effectively within specialised domains. This paper responds to a critical gap in the oil and gas industry characterised by the necessity to support on-site maintenance staff in failure diagnosis, spare parts selection, and implementation of specific maintenance procedures. This research presents the design, development, and evaluation of an Artificial Maintenance Agents Application (AMA-app). AMA-app enables users to upload maintenance details in various formats and incorporate external web resources as contextual information for their inquiries. It then processes these inquiries through a multi-agent system to generate responses by providing a step-by-step explanation of the reasoning process. The reported system uses Reflexion agent architecture in addition to chain of thoughts prompt engineering, hence providing a capability for processing diverse technical information inputs. The system integrates a reasoning mechanism for comprehending maintenance procedures and spare parts recommendations, in addition to performing an autonomous web search for the required spare parts. Finally, the app provides real-time web links for the required spare parts. The performance evaluation employed a qualitative research method centered on a focus group of maintenance experts to assess the app's usability. The focus group findings revealed strong technical accuracy of both answers and reasoning steps, with these features enhancing user confidence and comprehension. The paper concludes by highlighting the feasibility of developing maintenance-specific multi-agent system that prioritises LLMs as reasoning mechanisms in specialised fields.

title: A Comparative Performance Analysis: Vector Search vs Graph Databases for RAG Applications
authors: Nandi, Siva Prasad;Venganti, Vijayakumar;Soni, Vinay;Nutalapati, Venkat
source_name: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Systems and Emerging Technologies Icaiset 2026
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly critical in enterprise AI deployments, requiring efficient and semantically accurate retrieval mechanisms to supply Large Language Models (LLMs) with domain-specific context. While vector databases have emerged as the dominant paradigm for embedding-based retrieval, graph databases offer compelling advantages in explicit semantic relationship modeling and multi-hop reasoning across interconnected knowledge corpora. This paper presents a rigorous comparative performance analysis contrasting vector search systems specifically FAISS with HNSW indexing and Milvus against graph database retrieval using Neo4j, across three heterogeneous real-world datasets: Wikipedia QA (8.8M passages), PubMed biomedical abstracts (2.3M documents), and a financial regulatory corpus (500K documents). We evaluate across five performance dimensions: query latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (QPS), Recall@10, nDCG@10, and multi-hop reasoning accuracy. Our experimental results demonstrate that vector databases achieve 8.4ms median latency with 5,200 QPS throughput and a Recall@10 of 0.92 under high-volume semantic search workloads. In contrast, graph databases excel in relational reasoning, achieving 89% multi-hop accuracy versus 63% for vector approaches, at the cost of higher latency (31.2-52.3ms) and lower scalability (1,350 QPS at 1M documents, degrading to 920 QPS at 10M). We also examine Oracle Autonomous Database's unified AI Vector Search and Property Graph capabilities as a representative hybrid platform, discuss indexing strategies, embedding model selection, and graph construction methodologies, and derive actionable guidelines for RAG architects navigating technology selection.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Prompting Strategies for LLM-Based Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Chadli, Taha;Mourhir, Asmaa
source_name: 2026 6th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science Engineering and Technology Iraset 2026
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable performance on natural language understanding tasks but struggle with mathematical optimization problems, primarily due to calculation hallucinations and constraint tracking failures. The LLM-based Formalized Programming (LLMFP) framework addresses the above problems by shifting the role of the LLM from a solver to a translator that converts the natural language problems into executable Python code utilizing the Z3 solver. While the framework achieves up to 95% accuracy, its monolithic design introduces limitations such as error propagation, the lack of validation between stages, and parsing difficulties. Error analysis shows that the majority of LLMFP failures are due to formatting and parsing issues rather than reasoning errors. This paper presents the Parser-CoderValidator (PCV) technique, a three-stage modular architecture. The technique decomposes the optimization problem into three stages. First, we establish a new baseline through a comprehensive comparative analysis of the performance of the four state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-OSS-20B, GPT-OSS-120B, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Grok-Code-Fast-1) on 687 optimization problems across three problem domains: Coffee Supply Chain, Facility Location, and Workforce Scheduling. We then present a comparison of several prompting strategies, demonstrating that PCV achieves up to 39.71% overall accuracy improvements over the LLMFP baseline, with the most dramatic gains in Facility Location. The results underscore the significance of the PCV framework, which demonstrates that careful design of the prompting and validation process is as critical as model selection for achieving reliable LLM-based optimization.

title: Characterizing GPU Capacity and Computational Cost in Production AI Inference Using a Replica-Centric Measurement Framework
authors: Gupta, Ankur
source_name: Conference Proceedings 2026 IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for Industry 4 0 and Iot Metroind4 0 and Iot 2026
abstract: The rapid adoption of deep learning and large language models in production systems has fundamentally reshaped how large-scale platforms approach capacity planning. Unlike offline training workloads, online inference platforms must sustain strict latency, and availability guarantees under highly variable traffic while operating on scarce and expensive GPU resources. This paper presents a production-oriented capacity planning framework for GPU and Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) based AI inference platforms, derived from the design and operation of a global inference platform supporting inference services for retrieval and ranking pipelines at massive scale. The framework is replica-centric and explicitly incorporates planned disruption budgets, instance discriminators, GPU quotas, and system-level capacity buffers to balance fault tolerance, operational resilience, and utilization efficiency. We further examine real-world challenges such as hardware pool fragmentation, limited fault-domain diversity, and networking constraints, and describe pragmatic corrections for small workloads and constrained pools. The resulting approach enables predictable availability during routine operational events while materially improving GPU packing efficiency in production inference systems.

title: Design and Implementation of an RAG-Based Intelligent Maintenance Q&A System for Distributed Energy Storage Systems
authors: Bai, Baoyu;Bi, Jiayang;Chang, Jiashuo;Zhang, Delong;Yin, Jinliang
source_name: Proceedings 2026 IEEE 27th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and Its Applications Ccssta 2026
abstract: As the new power system is rapidly built and distributed energy storage is widely deployed, traditional operation & maintenance platforms face prominent drawbacks: high missed detection rates for equipment faults and low efficiency in tracing abnormal problems. Directly deploying generic large language models for energy storage maintenance easily leads to factual hallucinations, and these models cannot securely utilize private on-site industrial data.To address these limitations, this paper constructs a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) intelligent Q&A system tailored for distributed energy storage scenarios. We build a multi-source heterogeneous professional knowledge base covering maintenance specifications and historical fault records, and design a hybrid retrieval mechanism that fuses dense vector semantic search and BM25 keyword matching to strike a balance between deep semantic understanding and accurate professional term matching.Field verification based on multi-site engineering data demonstrates that the proposed hybrid-retrieval RAG system significantly improves diagnostic efficiency, enhances the accuracy of fault reasoning, and delivers reliable results for energy storage operation, maintenance and fault analysis.

title: Speak Your Network: Automated Network Emulation Construction with Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Orchestration
authors: Zou, Daolin;Xu, Jie;Luo, Long;Yu, Hongfang
source_name: IEEE International Workshop on Quality of Service Iwqos
abstract: Network research often relies on high fidelity emulation, but constructing greenfield environments still requires substantial manual effort. LLM agents face a gap between intent and implementation: long contexts, weak validation, and uniform model use make it difficult to translate intent into working emulator state. We present Nice, a closed-loop multi-agent framework that constructs greenfield emulations from natural language intents. Nice combines a hierarchical supervisor and worker architecture with context isolation, closed-loop verification for state grounding and self-healing, dual-layer experience memory, and adaptive LLM routing. On a 30-task benchmark, Nice increases success rate from 3.3% to 90.0%, reduces average model cost from 0.045 to 0.034 per task relative to the variant without routing, and improves first pass rate from 46.7% to 76.7%.

title: Sustainable AI-Enabled Supply Chain Architecture for Enhanced Communication and Decision Intelligence
authors: Hussain, S. Mahaboob;Malviya, Nishit;Pareek, Prakash;Reis, Manuel J.C.S.
source_name: Lecture Notes of the Institute for Computer Sciences Social Informatics and Telecommunications Engineering Lnicst
abstract: Traditional communication systems in supply chains face significant challenges in providing predictive analytics, real-time market and social insights. This often results in delays, suboptimal operational responses and substantial wastage of perishable goods. To address these limitations, we proposed an integrated AI-driven framework to minimize wastage and improve operational efficiency in perishable supply chains. This model combines social network analysis and market intelligence to enhance decision-making and stakeholder collaboration. We integrated Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, Large Language Models (LLMs), and optimization engines to deliver adaptive, data-centric insights along with real-time stakeholder data, stock market indicators. In this work, Prophet and XGBoost considered for adaptive demand forecasting, DistilBERT for text-based sentiment and entity analysis. Grok and Llama are utilized to generate multilingual, context-aware recommendations. Experimental validation demonstrates that the framework achieved a 32% median reduction in wastage and an 85% forecasting accuracy within Indian agri-food supply chains. Overall, this work delivers a scalable, sustainable, and intelligent solution aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 2, 9, 12, and 17), and sets the foundation for future quantum-enhanced supply chain systems.

title: QueueBreak: A Trace-to-Diagnosis Pipeline for Tail Latency in Agentic LLM Services
authors: Ma, Xingrao;Li, Zongxi;Dong, Chengzu;Shao, Di;Liu, Xiao
source_name: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Web Services Icws
abstract: Agentic large language model (LLM) services execute a user request as a workflow that interleaves model invocations with external tool calls. When workflow p99 grows, end-to-end latency alone cannot reveal whether the tail accumulates before execution starts or within execution; these regimes require different operational remedies. We present QueueBreak, a workflow-aware trace-to-diagnosis (T2D) framework that reconstructs request arrival, first-step start, and completion from lightweight workflow logs and step traces. QueueBreak decomposes each workflow before aggregating tail statistics, reports a Queue Dominance Signature, and checks the diagnosis through load-reduction intervention. Across load escalation, dependency degradation, and intervention, the evaluated service shows the same pattern: tail growth is dominated by pre-execution waiting while execution remains stable. In a mixed-workload sweep, total p99 rises from 21.25s to 165.40s as pre-execution p99 rises from 11.67s to 144.04s, whereas stress execution p99 is 16.80s. With tool failure (p<inf>fail</inf>=0.2), total p99 reaches 978.81s and the mean preexecution fraction reaches 0.923. Reducing load to one quarter of the stress rate cuts pre-execution p99 from 579.2s to 17.3s while execution p99 changes only from 18.0s to 17.5s. These results identify admission control and workflow-aware capacity planning as primary QoS recovery levers.

title: AI-Assisted Interactive Furniture Layout Optimization for Barrier-Free Living: A Hybrid LLM-Heuristic Approach
authors: Gatla, Nikhil;Walter, Christian Felix;Rogalski, Sven
source_name: Proceedings of the International Conference on Education and Research in Computer Aided Architectural Design in Europe
abstract: Designing barrier-free indoor environments demands strict adherence to accessibility regulations while accommodating diverse room geometries and furniture configurations. Conventional rule-based layout systems address this through explicit constraint encoding yet remain inherently rigid and incapable of producing generative layout suggestions beyond their programmed boundaries. This paper investigates the integration of large language models into an accessibility-aware furniture layout optimization framework, examining their capacity to internalize regulatory compliance patterns through fine-tuning on a synthetically generated dataset. Layout planning is formulated as a constrained optimization problem grounded in DIN 18040-2 accessibility standards. The proposed hybrid system combines a fine-tuned language model operating as a generative layout proposer with a deterministic rule-based geometric validator, establishing a decision-making hierarchy between probabilistic generation and exact compliance enforcement. The system is evaluated on a set of held-out room layouts, demonstrating a 46.0% average reduction in accessibility violations across 500 held-out test layouts. The paper further engages critically with the demonstrated capabilities and limitations of this approach, including the boundaries of geometric compliance as a representation of fully barrier-free spatial experience, and discusses the broader implications for AI-assisted design under regulatory constraints.

title: Design and Orchestration of Multi-Agent LLM Systems for Real-Time Enterprise Supply Chain Optimization
authors: Jingar, Nirmal Kumar
source_name: 2026 11th International Conference on Cloud Computing and Big Data Analytics Icccbda 2026
abstract: The current supply chain in corporate enterprises is highly dynamic and has features of volatility in demands, geopolitical uncertainties, transportation effects, and a rise in complexity of operations. Conventional centralized optimization, and single model AI solutions do not typically provide the flexibility and dynamism on the fly reasoning necessary to deal with such uncertainty. The paper will suggest a new supply chain Multi-Agent Large Language Model (MA-LLM) Supply Chain Orchestration System, which is capable of providing real-time, distributed, and intelligent decision-making on enterprise supply chain networks. The suggested system breaks down the operations of the supply chain into specialized reasoning agents, which are demand forecasting, inventory management, transportation planning, and risk assessment each being driven by Large Language Models and coordinated by a central orchestration system. The system coordinates relevant reasoning, cross-domain negotiation and global optimization to generate coordinated decisions, which consider the cost, service level and resiliency goals. According to the experimental comparisons with the other advanced AI-based supply chain models, including the LSTM-PSO Supply Chain Optimization Model and the ResilientAI-SCM with OptimX, the proposed approach has a high forecasting accuracy, low cost, high reliability, and high disruption response. Findings confirm that multi-agent LLM coordinate has a scalable and resilient answer to real-time enterprise supply chain optimization.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Grid-Scale Energy Storage Optimization: A Review
authors: Zhou, Chengwei;Gao, Mingxi;Wang, Rui;Liao, Zhenxiang
source_name: Proceeding 2026 Conference on Innovation and Technologies of Energy Storage Cites 2026
abstract: The rapid expansion of grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) is reshaping modern power systems under increasing renewable penetration. As storage simultaneously supports energy arbitrage, ancillary services, peak shaving, and renewable integration, conventional model-based optimization faces growing challenges in scalability and uncertainty. Artificial intelligence (AI), including deep learning, reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, federated learning, and large language models (LLMs), has emerged as a powerful tool for storage optimization. This review organizes recent advances into three areas: state perception, dispatch and scheduling, and capacity planning. Across these applications, AI has demonstrated substantial improvements in operational performance and planning efficiency, although results remain highly dependent on market conditions and system characteristics. Key challenges - including interpretability, safety, sim-to-real transfer, and cybersecurity - suggest that AI should complement rather than replace physics-based optimization. We conclude by highlighting future research directions in optimality, safety, and scalable deployment.

title: An Infrastructure-Aware Evaluation Model for LLM Token Output and Data Center Power Consumption
authors: Cao, Songzi;Yu, Zunpeng;Lian, Runze;Tong, Xiaoyu;Cao, Zixian;Wu, Lixia
source_name: 2026 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Industrial Technology Applications Aiita 2026
abstract: With the large-scale deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs), power consumption during the inference phase has become a critical bottleneck hindering the development of green Artificial Intelligence. Existing energy consumption estimation methods mostly simplify the relationship between Token output and power consumption as linear, and generally overlook data center infrastructure overhead as well as the heterogeneity between Prefill and Decode phases during inference, leading to insufficient estimation accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Infrastructure-Aware Evaluation Model, aiming to achieve accurate quantitative evaluation of LLM Token output and data center power consumption. The model first decomposes the inference process into the compute-intensive Prefill phase and the memory-intensive Decode phase, establishing energy consumption benchmarks respectively. Secondly, it introduces multi-dimensional correction factors including input/output length, Batch Size, and quantization precision to characterize nonlinear energy consumption fluctuations caused by dynamic load changes. Finally, it integrates regional infrastructure parameters such as data center PUE and carbon intensity to achieve end-to-end conversion from chip-level power consumption to total data center power consumption. Extensive experiments based on public datasets covering more than 70 mainstream models demonstrate that the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of the model can be as low as 4.07%, significantly outperforming traditional linear models. Furthermore, this paper quantitatively identifies the energy efficiency 'Sweet Spot' of LLM inference for the first time, confirming the natural advantage of the MoE architecture in energy efficiency. This research provides important quantitative support for data center capacity planning, green load scheduling, and model energy efficiency evaluation.

title: Enhancing Scoping Reviews with Large Language Models : Iterative Prompt and Script Engineering for Venture Capital Investment Strategy Research
authors: Arendas, Csaba;Haidegger, Tamas P.;Zrubka, Zsombor
source_name: Ines 2026 2026 IEEE 30th Jubilee International Conference on Intelligent Engineering Systems Proceedings
abstract: The volume of academic publications continues to expand rapidly, making scoping reviews and systematic mapping studies increasingly labour-intensive. In Venture Capital (VC) investment research the stakes are particularly high because only a small fraction of VC-backed companies generates exceptional returns and many VC funds underperform public markets. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology for enhancing scoping reviews using Large Language Models (LLMs), with a specific focus on prompt engineering and API-based script development. Building on prior work that introduced an LLM-assisted classification pipeline for VC investment strategies, the evolution from simple web-based prompts through agent-mode experimentation to a large-scale, reproducible API workflow is documented. The study draws on detailed research logs and iterative experiments using multiple LLMs - OpenAI GPT-4o, Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Google Gemini 2.5 Pro - to classify thousands of VC-related publications into hierarchical tiers. The impact of different prompt designs, including the removal of a tertiary category, on classification outcomes is evaluated, as is the effectiveness of script refinements in mitigating rate-limit errors. Experimental results show that the final ensemble pipeline achieves high inter-model agreement (98.9 %) and dramatically reduces manual screening effort, offering a reproducible template for future scoping reviews. Methodological contributions, limitations and broader implications for integrating AI into venture capital research are discussed.

title: Salience of GenAI and student demand for college majors: Evidence from U.S. degree completions
authors: Peng, Gang
source_name: Journal of Education for Business
abstract: This study examines how the rising salience of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly the diffusion of large language model tools such as ChatGPT, is associated with changes in student demand for majors in U.S. higher education. Using data from the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) for 2020–2024, with 2022 as the pre/post base year, we link 1,140 academic majors to a GenAI Exposure index that captures the fraction of occupational tasks performable by large language models and compare trends before and after 2022. Majors with higher GenAI Exposure exhibit significantly larger degree completions after 2022, while pre-2022 completion trends are parallel across exposure groups. This supports a complementarity interpretation: students view GenAI as an opportunity rather than a threat. Business schools should respond by expanding analytics, data science, and AI-integrated programs.

title: A Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Disaster Image Summarization
authors: Yoshizaki, Hibiki;Uchiyama, Akira;Hiromori, Akihito;Takai, Mineo;Yamaguchi, Hirozumi
source_name: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications Workshops Percom Workshops
abstract: During disasters, response agencies must rapidly obtain accurate situational awareness. Images of on-site conditions are useful for this purpose, but their large data size makes real-time aggregation from many locations difficult when communication infrastructure is degraded. We address this challenge by combining a disaster-ready wide-area wireless system (DR-IoT) with small edge devices deployed across sites. Each device locally summarizes captured images into concise text and transmits the text as a compressed proxy, enabling objective reporting and efficient multi-site data collection under strict bandwidth limits. We develop a lightweight model that runs on small devices and generates textual summaries of disaster scenes. title: Aggregate Local, Sync Global: A Hierarchical Approach to Efficient Geo-Distributed LLM Training
authors: De Luca, Francesco;De Nadai, Francesco;Scazzariello, Mariano;Caiazzi, Tommaso;Farshin, Alireza;Chiesa, Marco;Di Battista, Giuseppe
source_name: Proceedings IEEE INFOCOM
abstract: Nowadays, the exponential growth of LLMs in size, increasingly stringent data sovereignty regulations, and growing power and energy constraints in modern datacenters are driving the adoption of multi-datacenter infrastructures to distribute the training process. However, standard training frameworks prove ill-suited for these heterogeneous environments, lacking awareness of inter-datacenter constraints or stretching communication patterns across sites without differentiating between network tiers. This approach causes severe bottlenecks on high-latency inter-datacenter links, hindering scalability. To address this challenge, we propose a hierarchical communication strategy designed to decouple intra-site aggregation from global synchronization through the election of "leader model replicas". Experimental results show that the proposed hierarchical strategy reduces training iteration time by up to 32% and exposed communication time by up to 65% compared to the baseline Megatron-LM strategy, providing an effective solution for scaling training workloads across geographically distributed datacenters.

title: A Hierarchical Framework for Enterprise-Scale Aspect Extraction from Code-Switched E-Commerce Reviews: A Comparative Deployment Study
authors: Dionela, Valiant Lance D.;Dy, Fatima Kriselle S.;Hombrebueno, Robin James M.;Nicolas, Aaron Rae M.;Cheng, Charibeth K.;Gonda, Raphael W.
source_name: International Conference on Enterprise Information Systems Iceis Proceedings
abstract: E-commerce platforms in multilingual markets struggle to extract actionable insights from code-switched reviews. Filipino platforms such as Shopee process millions of “Taglish” (Tagalog-English) reviews annually without automated tools for aspect-level analysis. This study presents a decision support framework for aspect extraction in low-resource, code-switched environments. A Hierarchical Aspect Framework (HAF), developed through topic modeling triangulation, organizes feedback into 4 general and 21 specific business categories. To support technology selection for enterprise deployment, four distinct approaches are compared: (1) Rule-Based systems, (2) Generative Large Language Models (Gemini 2.0 Flash), and (3) two fine-tuned Gemma-3 models trained using different annotation strategies. Evaluated on 10,510 real-world reviews, the generative LLM achieves an F1 score of 91%, excelling at implicit aspects, while rule-based systems offer up to 70% cost reduction for high-volume tasks. Fine-tuned models show limited viability due to capacity constraints. A cost-benefit analysis further indicates that hybrid deployment strategies can reduce manual review analysis costs by approximately 85% while maintaining enterprise-grade accuracy. The proposed framework enables a scalable, linguistically adaptive customer intelligence solution, with applications in product development, customer service, and competitive analysis across Southeast Asian e-commerce.
