title: A Hybrid Generative AI and Optimization Approach for Resilient Emergency Department Layouts
authors: Manae, Othman;Bouramtane, Khalil;Kharraja, Said;Riffi, Jamal;El Beqqali, Omar
source_name: 12th 2026 International Conference on Control Decision and Information Technologies Codit 2026
abstract: Effective spatial organization in hospital emergency departments (EDs) is critical for delivering timely patient care and minimizing operational inefficiencies. Instead of relying on human judgment or traditional optimization methods, which may not adapt well to changing healthcare systems, this work proposes a hybrid method of combining a large language model (LLM) with an optimized algorithm to automate and improve hospital department layouts. The framework incorporates key spatial and operational criteria, including patient flows between rooms, inter-room distances, room priority levels and the most important are the health crises constraints. The LLM acts as a constraint-aware symbolic generator used to initialize the optimization stage that produces clinically plausible room-function reassignments from a structured JSON representation of the layout, sanitary and operational constraints, and scientific knowledge retrieved via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). These LLM-generated proposals are then refined by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), which optimize flow-weighted distance costs, reassignment penalties, room priorities, and feasibility requirements. Our contribution focuses on integrating LLM-based reasoning with optimization techniques to improve solutions to the healthcare facility layout problem (FLP). By comparing widely used optimization algorithms for healthcare facilities, we evaluate the effectiveness of our integrated approach. Our experimental results from our simulated ED with realistic hospital constraints indicate increased spatial and functional efficiency over the existing baseline layout. The simulated emergency department in this study is inspired by the organization of a hospital emergency unit in Roanne.

title: Collective Intelligence Optimization: Coordinating Large-Scale Multi-Agent AI Systems for Scalable Distributed Learning
authors: Tewari, Rahul;Prasath Manoharan, Balaje;Vishwanath Chincholi, Tarun;Prakash Pandey, Chandra
source_name: 2026 International Conference on Computing Theory and Wireless Communications Icctwc 2026
abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in enterprise environments has introduced new challenges in security, compliance, and automation across the DevOps lifecycle. Traditional perimeter-based security mechanisms are no longer adequate for distributed model pipelines that span cloud, edge, and hybrid infrastructures. This paper explores the application of Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles to automate DevOps workflows for LLM deployment and maintenance. It presents a layered framework that enforces continuous verification, micro-segmentation, and least-privilege policies throughout model training, CI/CD pipelines, and inference services. A modular automation strategy is proposed, integrating policy-as-code, secure API orchestration, and identity-aware access management for end-to-end model governance. Through architectural analysis and simulated DevSecOps scenarios, the study demonstrates that Zero Trust-driven automation significantly enhances the resilience, observability, and scalability of LLM production systems while reducing human intervention and compliance risk. The work bridges operational efficiency with proactive security, offering a unified blueprint for safe and automated AI deployment pipelines.

title: Corporate Case Study: Evaluation of ML and LLM-Based Approaches
authors: Tural, Büşra;Alp, Erva;Destan, Zeynep
source_name: Isades 2026 2nd International Symposium on AI Driven Engineering Systems Proceedings
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has led to the widespread use of generative AI approaches, particularly those based on Large Language Model (LLM) and Small Language Model (SLM), in both academic studies and enterprise transformation projects. Successful results in areas such as natural language processing (NLP), document analysis, content generation, and decision support systems have made large-scale language models a priority technology for many organizations. However, attempting to solve every problem with generative AI-based architectures brings with it various technical challenges in terms of high processing power requirements, operational costs, explainability problems, latency, and sustainability. This study argues that technology selection in enterprise AI projects should be evaluated not only based on current trends or model popularity, but also in accordance with the nature of the problem and operational needs. It is considered that traditional machine learning (ML) methods offer significant advantages in terms of low cost, high performance, faster operation, and explainability, especially in prediction, scoring, anomaly detection, classification, and operational decision support processes. The article also examines, through an institutional case study, how classical ML algorithms can produce more efficient, sustainable, and successful results in some projects initially planned with an LLM/SLM-based design. Accordingly, it is shown that hybrid and engineering-oriented architectures, shaped according to the problem type, can provide more effective solutions in AI projects than a 'single model approach.' The study emphasizes that success in AI projects depends not on the size of the model used, but on establishing the right balance between accuracy, cost, performance, explainability, and sustainability.

title: Embodied Intelligent Agents for Adaptive Logistics Scheduling in Power Equipment Supply Networks
authors: Gao, Chaoxia;Qi, Shucheng
source_name: Isades 2026 2nd International Symposium on AI Driven Engineering Systems Proceedings
abstract: To address challenges such as seasonal demand fluctuations, imbalance between bulk and low-value materials, and the slow response of traditional optimization methods in modern power systems, this study proposes a hierarchical embodied multi-agent scheduling framework (HEMAS). The framework integrates macro semantic cognition, meso-level coordination, and micro physical execution. At the cloud layer, a large language model (LLM) acts as a supply chain planning agent for demand forecasting and cross-domain negotiation under disruptions. At the edge layer, a heterogeneous graph neural network-based multi-agent reinforcement learning method (HGNN-MAPPO) is used for real-time routing and scheduling. At the physical layer, a vision-language-action (VLA) model enables embodied execution of logistics equipment, supported by an Embodied Context Protocol (ECP) for heterogeneous device coordination.Experiments in a high-fidelity digital twin environment show that, compared with ILSO and single-agent reinforcement learning (S-RL), HEMAS improves vehicle load factor to 86.4%, reduces total logistics cost by 28.7%, and achieves an on-time delivery rate of 98.3%. Under sudden supply chain disruptions, the system recovery time is reduced to 4.2 seconds. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating embodied AI with hierarchical multi-agent scheduling for resilient and efficient power logistics systems.

title: Intersection of Quantum Computing and Machine Learning
authors: Nellikondi, Raghavendar
source_name: Quantum Machine Learning Revolutionizing Data Analysis and Optimization
abstract: Quantum machine learning is the use of quantum computers to perform machine learning tasks. Also, it can assist with large data sets and unstructured data. QML systems could enhance machine learning and enable new means of data analysis by leveraging quantum mechanics principles such as entanglement, interference, and superposition. This section discusses the state of the art with respect to hybrid quantum models, fully quantum algorithms, quantum-assisted traditional learning, and other varieties. Applications range from drug discovery to supply-chain optimisation, cyber safety and natural language processing. While QML has the possibility to be a game-changer, there are many roadblocks such as quantum decoherence, data encoding issues, and algorithms not maturing. These problems require coordinated incremental advances in hardware, algorithm design, and theory to resolve. This paper does all the essential background work that provides significant concepts, status of ongoing implementation and major algorithms, security and compliance landscape of QML that would help in looking into the future of QML.

authors: Kenne, Modeste M.;Chio, Andrew;Hu, Zheng Hui;Rousseau, Julie;Venkatasubramanian, Nalini
source_name: Proceedings 2026 IEEE International Conference on Smart Computing Smartcomp 2026
abstract: Prolonged power outages pose a significant threat to the continuity of critical healthcare services. Enhancing resilience requires integrating hazard exposures, infrastructure dependencies, and operational constraints into actionable preparedness plans. We present BlackOps, a decision-support framework developed with input from healthcare and hazard analytics experts. The system integrates GIS data on facility locations, hazard footprints, power grids, and road networks to assess vulnerability. To bridge the gap between policy and practice, we leverage context-aware Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract facility-specific required autonomy (operational self-sufficiency under grid failure) and metadata from unstructured regulatory documents. Beyond regulatory compliance, BlackOps quantifies preparedness through indices that measure a facility’s ability to replenish resources from regional partners, while accounting for stochastic grid failures and structural damage. These metrics are aggregated into a unified risk score and translated into facility scorecards. These outputs provide decision makers with priority tiers and actionable insights, such as supplemental energy requirements and optimal resource pre-staging locations. Experiments across thousands of scenarios demonstrate the framework’s ability to enhance healthcare resilience during multi-day outages.

title: BlochShift: Physics-Guided Diffusion with Bloch-Based Drift for MRI Image Translation
authors: Wang, Zihao;Gan, Yu;Wu, Ona
source_name: 2026 IEEE 15th Image Video and Multidimensional Signal Processing Workshop Ivmsp 2026
abstract: Multi-contrast MRI improves diagnostic workflows, but comprehensive protocols are frequently unavailable due to scan-time limits and site-dependent acquisition variability. We study paired T1 ↔ T2 MRI translation under multi-site scanner/protocol shift with an emphasis on few-step inference suitable for clinical pipelines. We propose BlochShift, a physicsguided diffusion formulation that introduces trajectory-level cross-domain control by (i) constructing a spatially varying domain-mixture field from simplified Bloch-derived signal models and coarse tissue priors, and (ii) injecting its closed-form time derivative as an explicit restoration drift in the reverse-time dynamics. This stepwise drift pulls each denoising update toward target-consistent contrast and reduces translation drift under large integration steps. Experiments on the multi-center IXI dataset show that BlochShift achieves SSIM/PSNR =0.75 / 23.13 for T 1 T 2 and 0.83 / 24.18 for T 2 T 1, outperforming GAN and diffusion-bridge baselines in both directions.

title: SEGA: A Stepwise Evolution Paradigm for Content-Aware Layout Generation with Design Prior
authors: Wang, Haoran;Zhao, Bo;Wang, Jinghui;Wang, Hanzhang;Yang, Huan;Ji, Wei;Liu, Hao;Xiao, Xinyan
source_name: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
abstract: In this paper, we study the content-aware layout generation problem, which aims to automatically generate layouts that are harmonious with a given background image. Existing methods usually deal with this task with a single-step reasoning framework. The lack of a feedback-based selfcorrection mechanism leads to their failure rates significantly increasing when faced with complex element layout planning. To address this challenge, we introduce SEGA, a novel Stepwise Evolution Paradigm for Content-Aware Layout GenerAtion. Inspired by the systematic mode of human thinking, SEGA employs a hierarchical reasoning framework with a coarse-to-fine strategy: first, a coarselevel module roughly estimates the layout planning results; then, another refining module performs fine-level reasoning regarding the coarse planning results. Furthermore, we incorporate layout design principles as prior knowledge into the model to enhance its layout planning ability. Besides, we present GenPoster-100K that is a new largescale poster dataset with rich meta-information annotation. The experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by achieving the state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmark datasets. Our project page is at: https://brucew91.github.io/SEGA.github.io/

title: Understanding the causal dynamics of risk factors in sustainable urban-rural integration: a stage-dependent fuzzy analysis approach
authors: He, Lei; Zhu, Yuming; Zheng, Xin; Mu, Bingxu
source_name: ENGINEERING CONSTRUCTION AND ARCHITECTURAL MANAGEMENT
abstract: Purpose This study aims to decipher the dynamic risk evolution mechanism in urban–rural integration development public projects (URID-PPs). It addresses the limitations of static assessments by analyzing how risks propagate across planning, implementation and operational stages to enhance project resilience. Design/methodology/approach A stage-dependent analytical framework is developed. Large language models (LLMs) are integrated with grounded theory to systematically identify risk factors. To address uncertainty in expert judgment, ELICIT-based linguistic processing is employed, and a hybrid fuzzy BWM and dynamic fuzzy DEMATEL approach is used to quantify factor importance and capture evolving causal relationships across the project lifecycle. Findings Results reveal distinct evolutionary trajectories: institutional risks dominate the planning phase as root causes, while coordination friction escalates during implementation. In the operational phase, risks shift toward endogenous market mechanisms. Eleven critical risk factors, such as inadequate cross-departmental coordination, are identified, exhibiting stage-specific causal behaviors. Originality/value This study advances the research on URID-PPs by moving beyond conventional static risk assessments and introducing a stage-dependent perspective that captures the temporal heterogeneity of risk evolution. By integrating LLM-assisted qualitative analysis and ELICIT information expression, the proposed approach enhances both the systematic identification of risk factors and the rigorous handling of uncertainty in expert judgment. Furthermore, the study reveals how risk causal structures dynamically evolve across different project stages, offering a more nuanced understanding of risk propagation mechanisms and providing an analytical basis for adaptive, stage-specific governance in complex public projects.

title: Effect of baking temperature on an organic-inorganic hybrid coating for magnesium alloy AZ31B
authors: Cao, Xianlong; Wei, Yanjiang; Ren, Quanyou; Zhan, Xun; Liao, Shuting; Wang, Ruonan
source_name: ANTI-CORROSION METHODS AND MATERIALS
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to systematically investigate the effect of baking temperature on the morphology, thickness, adhesion and corrosion resistance of an organic-inorganic hybrid coating applied to magnesium alloy AZ31B, trying to elucidate the intrinsic curing-temperature-response mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach A homogeneous organic-inorganic hybrid coating was prepared on magnesium alloy AZ31B using the sol–gel technique with tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxy silane (GPTMS) and triethylene tetramine (TETA). The influence of various baking temperatures (80 °C–130 °C) on the coatings were evaluated through scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy, optical microscopy (OM), X-ray diffraction pattern (XRD), thickness measurements, scratch adhesion tests and electrochemical methods including potentiodynamic polarization and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Findings The hybrid coating was mainly composed of amorphous SiO2. The hybrid coating showed dense microstructure, uniform thickness (∼20 µm) and intimate interfacial adhesion at the baking temperature of 110 °C, and significantly improved the corrosion resistance of the magnesium alloy, reducing the corrosion current density by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to the uncoated substrate. While adhesion gradually deteriorated with increasing temperature, optimal corrosion resistance and adhesion were achieved at 110 °C, where protection efficiency reached (98.5 ± 0.4)%. This is attributed to enhanced cross-linking density and barrier properties, despite the gradual adhesion loss. At higher temperatures (130 °C), microcrack formation due to excessive internal stress led to deteriorated coating integrity and corrosion performance, with protection efficiency dropping to (84.5 ± 1.1)%. Practical implications The identified optimal curing temperature (110 °C) provides coating lines with a simple, readily implementable parameter. This process requires no complex compositional modifications, enabling manufacturers to achieve cost-effective production scale-up, reduced energy consumption and enhanced product durability without additional capital investment. Social implications Enhanced corrosion protection extends magnesium component lifespans, reducing material waste and resource consumption. Lightweighting enabled by durable magnesium alloys contributes to lower vehicle emissions and improved energy efficiency, supporting global sustainability goals and environmental protection. Originality/value This work elucidates the competing mechanisms between coating densification and adhesion degradation during thermal curing of GPTMS/TEOS/TETA-based hybrid coatings. It reveals that optimal protection at 110 °C is achieved when barrier property enhancement outweighs adhesion loss, prior to microcracking-dominated failure. This work provides a foundational understanding of process–performance relationships, which is essential for designing more complex coating systems.

title: Multi-Model Stacking Ensemble with Multi-Perspective Interpretability Analysis for Solar Power Forecasting
authors: Wu, Shijie; Lin, Dejing; Zhang, Yushuai
source_name: ENERGIES
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is important for grid dispatch, energy-storage management, and electricity-market trading. This paper presents a PV power forecasting framework that combines multi-model ensemble learning with multi-perspective interpretability analysis. A 22-dimensional feature set was constructed from irradiance, meteorological, temporal, and lagged-power variables. Five supervised regressors, a zero-shot Chronos-Bolt-Small time-series foundation model, and six additional forecasting baselines were evaluated at two PV plants. The three ensemble schemes used only the five supervised regressors and were compared on the final 20% of the 2019 development data; the complete 2020 period was used only for final evaluation. The selected methods achieved normalized RMSE values of 0.0350 and 0.0376 at Sites 1 and 2, respectively. SHAP, PDP/ICE, LIME, and permutation importance were applied to the ensemble model at each site. Recent power-history features dominated this one-step-ahead forecasting task with a 15 min horizon, while irradiance features provided additional site-dependent information.

title: Multi-Scale 3D Network Visualization for Large-Scale Coordinated Operations with Organizational Hierarchy
authors: Wang, Jiachen; Cheng, Cheng-Yu; Zhao, Qi; Liu, Hang; Chen, Genshe
source_name: SENSORS AND SYSTEMS FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS XIX
abstract: Large-scale coordinated operations—such as disaster response, multisite logistics, remote industrial operations, and multi-agency public-safety missions—rely on heterogeneous wireless networks in which each node may carry multiple radio interfaces spanning satellite, cellular, mesh, and land-mobile radio technologies. Visualizing these networks is challenging because analysts must simultaneously reason about multibearer connectivity, organizational hierarchy, and geospatial context, often across thousands of nodes and under time pressure. Existing tools typically address these domains in isolation: network visualizers lack organizational context, while geospatial platforms do not natively support multi-layer topology overlay. This paper presents a unified, web-based visualization and analysis platform that addresses three core challenges. First, scalable rendering of heterogeneous connectivity, achieved through a coverage-based geometric model and WebGPU-accelerated GPU-instanced rendering that maintains interactive frame rates at scales of thousands to tens of thousands of nodes. Second, integrated display of topology and organizational hierarchy within a single workspace, with linked navigation across a 3D geospatial view (globe, map, and tactical scales) and an organizational tree panel. Third, timely information delivery through temporal replay of network state snapshots and an LLM-based summarization layer that produces concise natural-language briefs of salient state changes—node movements, link formations, coverage shifts—without requiring operators to inspect every event manually. Demonstrations on representative deployment scenarios show that the platform supports real-time situational awareness and analysis tasks requiring simultaneous understanding of hierarchical, topological, and spatial relationships at operational scale.

title: Application of Generative AI in Industry 5.0: A Fictional SME Case Study
authors: van Erp, Tim; Pereira, Bruno; McMurray, Adela
source_name: SAFE AND SUSTAINABLE VALUE CREATION BY DESIGN, GCSM 2025, VOL 2
abstract: Novel generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) tools are increasingly being introduced to the marketplace, offering new opportunities for manufacturing companies. Often, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) struggle to navigate the landscape of newly released software solutions due to a lack of AI competencies and limited resources for technology scouting. This qualitative research discusses a novel and fictional SME case study for combining multiple genAI tools to reduce the time-to-market of new products significantly. The case study covers ideation, computer-aided design (CAD), and computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) as relevant manufacturing phases for SMEs engaged in New Product Development. Based on the case study, a critical discussion of Industry 5.0 benefits and barriers to using genAI in manufacturing is presented. Ultimately, the research contributes to fostering a culture of innovation by demonstrating a novel combination of genAI tools to support the design-for-manufacturing process. This can significantly decrease the time-to-market and improve the return-on-investment, competitive advantage, and potentially a transition towards Industry 5.0 if the barriers to genAI adoption are overcome.

title: AI-Driven Hybrid Edge-Cloud Architecture for Real-Time Big Data Analytics and Scalable Communication in Retail Supply Chains
authors: Ratra, Karan Kumar; Seth, Dhruv Kumar
source_name: SOUTHEASTCON 2025
abstract: There are various challenges that the retail sector faces these days, and these include the fluctuating customer trends, poor inventory management especially when dealing with multiple channels, and language barriers. This paper proposes an AI-enabled Hybrid Edge-to-Cloud Infrastructure as the right solution to the challenges in the retail supply chain. This solution will streamline the data visualization and communication and increase the efficiency of the communication while at the same time improving the inventory demand forecasting. The combination of AI algorithms and a mix of models into one platform will transform the supply chain by offering direct solutions to current inefficiencies. The fabric has self-learning AI algorithms on the edge to react to changing demand patterns to enable localized decision-making for replenishment inventory items and accurate demand forecasting for last-mile delivery planning. In cloud computing technology solutions, generative AI creates scenarios-based models for longer-term planning and multi-channel communication for cross-functional collaboration. An advanced hierarchy-based blending feature makes it easy to sync edge and cloud operations without losing time transmitting data or making real-time decisions. The platform also consists of AI-advanced communication protocols focusing on data flow for reliable information flow across supply chain networks. It uses shortened technical language and prioritizes outcome-driven practical gains and action. Using real-world cases and actual implementations, this model exhibits fewer supply chain failures, more consistent demand and supply alignment, and significant savings. By confronting them with novel solutions, this research is an innovation-driven case study for retail supply chains to see how the AI fusion of edge and cloud can improve efficiency, agility, and scale to address dynamic challenges.

title: Copying style, Extracting value: Illustrators' Perception of AI Style Transfer and its Impact on Creative Labor
authors: Porquet, Julien; Wang, Sitong; Chilton, Lydia B.
source_name: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2025 CHI CONFERENCE ON HUMAN FACTORS IN COMPUTING SYTEMS, CHI 2025
abstract: Generative text-to-image models are disrupting the lives of creative professionals. Specifically, illustrators are threatened by models that claim to extract and reproduce their style. Yet, research on style transfer has rarely focused on their perspectives. We provided four illustrators with a model fine-tuned to their style and conducted semi-structured interviews about the model's successes, limitations, and potential uses. Evaluating their output, artists reported that style transfer successfully copies aesthetic fragments but is limited by content-style disentanglement and lacks the crucial emergent quality of their style. They also deemed the others' copies more successful. Understanding the results of style transfer as "boundary objects," we analyze how they can simultaneously be considered unsuccessful by artists and poised to replace their work by others. We connect our findings to critical HCI frameworks, demonstrating that style transfer, rather than merely a Creativity Support Tool, should also be understood as a supply chain optimization one.

title: Relevance of Topics in Workflow-Based Student Projects
authors: Dannecker, A.; Meyer, L.
source_name: BUSINESS PROCESS MANAGEMENT: BLOCKCHAIN, ROBOTIC PROCESS AUTOMATION, CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPEAN, EDUCATORS AND INDUSTRY FORUM: BPM 2024 BLOCKCHAIN, RPA, CEE, EDUCATORS AND INDUSTRY FORUM
abstract: One of the significant challenges today involves developing innovative teaching concepts for business students in the field of digitalization. At the beginning of their studies, students usually only know the basics of IT, primarily related to their personal (mobile) environments, rather than real business scenarios such as business process management or workflow management. This paper explores an innovative teaching concept in the digitalization field for business students. It focuses on how students perceive process automation in workflows using tools like Camunda, especially when tasks involve artificial intelligence (AI) components and decision models (DMN). In this paper, we discuss the decision criteria relevant to the selection of an automation task for business students, examining the criteria students use to choose topics—whether based on difficulty, topic selection (such as supplier selection, project evaluation, product development, etc.), or the relevance to DMN and AI. Additionally, we compare whether there are differences in topic selection between Vietnamese and Swiss students.
